english.title: Fail to ensure that premises other than slaughterhouse for killing animals were suitable
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the business operator in respect of premises, other than a slaughterhouse, used for the killing of animals, namely **(..SPECIFY PREMISES..), failed to ensure that

(A)_[it had suitable equipment and facilities available for the purpose of unloading animals from means of transport]_
(B)_[there were no sharp edges or protrusions with which an animal may have come into contact]_
(C)_[the place of killing was sited in such a way as to minimise handling of the animal at any time up to the point of killing]_
(D)_[any instrument, restraining equipment, other equipment or installation which was used for stunning or killing was designed, constructed and maintained so as to facilitate rapid and effective stunning or killing]_
(E)_[any defect found in back-up stunning or killing equipment was rectified forthwith]_

in that **(..SPECIFY FAILURE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 30(1)(d) and 33(1) of, and paragraph 4 of Schedule 2 to, the Welfare of Animals at the Time of Killing (England) Regulations 2015.

other.penalty:
Summary: Fine

Time limit for prosecutions
6 monthsNote
Note that for offences committed since 12 March 2015, section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012 removes the limits on certain fines given by the Magistrates' Courts. Offences that were previously punishable by fines of 'prescribed sums' and that were limited to 'not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale' or 'not exceeding the statutory maximum', are now punishable by a fine of any amount.
